title: CustomGPT Creation

numberingPolicy.summary: Use simple linear numbering for the rebuilt workshop deck and keep the back half reserved for the live walkthrough block.
notes: Keep numbering stable once the workshop narrative is locked.
Reserve the back half for the live build and testing walkthrough.

narrativeSpine: Administrative policy lookup in residency is slow, repetitive, and frustrating.
A custom GPT can become a grounded policy assistant if instructions and source files are designed carefully.
The audience should leave knowing what to build, how to test it, and how to govern it safely.

slides.title: Workshop Title and Promise
slides.purpose: Open the talk, establish presenters, and frame the workshop promise.
slides.subheader: Designing a practical custom GPT for residency administration support
slides.takeaway: This workshop will show what the tool is, why it works, and how to build one.
slides.figureRole: Orient the audience with title, presenters, and workshop structure.
slides.selectedDirection: Title-promise v1 is the current selected opener.
notes: Use this as the clean typographic opener while the rest of the workshop visual language settles.

variants.label: Title Promise V1
variants.summary: Typographic opener that uses the SAEM palette and a three-step workshop promise panel.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.purpose: Show the administrative pain point and why the audience should care immediately.
slides.header: Policy questions keep landing on the same people
slides.subheader: Program directors, chiefs, coordinators, and residents repeatedly search static documents for operational answers
slides.takeaway: This is a workflow problem worth fixing, not just a novelty demo.
slides.figureRole: Make the administrative burden tangible without overloading the audience.
slides.selectedDirection: Workflow-burden v1 is the current selected problem frame.
notes: This replaces a denser theory-first opening with a direct operational burden frame.

variants.label: Workflow Burden V1
variants.summary: Two-panel burden slide showing the people who absorb policy lookup work and the repeated question loop they face.

slides.title: What This Tool Is
slides.purpose: Define the product plainly before theory.
slides.header: A custom GPT can act like a residency policy assistant
slides.subheader: It answers questions using uploaded policies, instructions, and selected capabilities inside ChatGPT
slides.takeaway: The audience should understand the object before hearing how it is built.
slides.figureRole: Show a concrete input/output example of a grounded policy answer.
slides.selectedDirection: Policy-assistant-object v1 is the current selected concept card.
notes: Keep the example clearly illustrative so it teaches the object without implying specific institutional policy.

variants.label: Policy Assistant Object V1
variants.summary: Question-to-answer concept card that shows the assistant as a grounded policy Q&A workflow before the build walkthrough.

slides.title: Why It Works
slides.purpose: Explain the mechanism without drowning the audience in transformer theory.
slides.header: Good policy assistants are configured, grounded ChatGPT workflows
slides.subheader: Instructions guide behavior, knowledge files provide source material, and capabilities extend what the GPT can do
slides.takeaway: This is enough conceptual depth for the workshop audience.
slides.figureRole: Use a simple three-part system diagram rather than a dense technical stack.

slides.title: What Good Looks Like
slides.purpose: Define the output standard before the walkthrough.
slides.header: A good answer is specific, sourced, and bounded
slides.subheader: The assistant should answer from the documents, cite its source, and say when it does not know
slides.takeaway: This slide sets the quality bar for the live demo.
slides.figureRole: Show a policy question paired with a good answer and a bad answer.

slides.title: Source Prep
slides.purpose: Show the file and knowledge design decisions that matter most.
slides.header: The files matter as much as the model
slides.subheader: Clear, current, text-forward policy documents improve retrieval and reduce confusion
slides.takeaway: Knowledge quality and instruction quality are the real implementation work.
slides.figureRole: Make document prep concrete and non-technical.

slides.title: Live Walkthrough Setup
slides.purpose: Start the live build with a clear map of the steps.
slides.header: We are about to build the assistant live
slides.subheader: Create the GPT, define the instructions, upload files, test it, then refine it
slides.takeaway: The audience should know what to watch for in the demo.
slides.figureRole: Provide a clean agenda card for the walkthrough block.

slides.title: Live Build
slides.purpose: Walk through the current GPT creation surface in ChatGPT.
slides.subheader: Use the GPTs area, choose Create, then work through configuration directly
slides.takeaway: The workshop should focus on the actual current UI, not the old product assumptions.
slides.figureRole: Use annotated interface screenshots rather than abstract diagrams.

slides.title: Live Testing
slides.purpose: Demonstrate preview testing, refusals, and source-bounded answers.
slides.header: Testing matters more than builder theatrics
slides.subheader: A good workshop demo should show a strong answer, a weak answer, and an explicit refusal
slides.takeaway: Testing is where trust is earned.
slides.figureRole: Compare good and bad preview interactions with callouts.

slides.title: Governance and Maintenance
slides.purpose: Land the operational rules for safe use.
slides.header: The tool needs ownership, updates, and clear boundaries
slides.subheader: No PHI, current documents only, citations expected, and a named owner for updates
slides.takeaway: This is the adult supervision slide.
slides.figureRole: Summarize governance in a compact card set.

slides.title: Takeaways and Q&A
slides.purpose: Close with memorable decisions, not more theory.
slides.header: Build small, ground it well, test it hard
slides.subheader: Custom GPTs can reduce administrative friction when they are well-scoped and well-governed
slides.takeaway: Leave the audience with a practical next step and discussion prompts.
slides.figureRole: Clean closing summary with optional QR or link area.
